speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are an 8-month-old boy experiencing feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To help me understand your condition better, can you tell me if you are gaining weight normally and have you noticed any vomiting or blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: The baby is fussy with feeding difficulties and a visibly distended abdomen that worsens with palpation. Has he been passing gas or stool normally, and is there any history of a specific "whoops" sound during feeding?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Good, no signs of infection. Did the baby pass meconium within 24 hours of birth, and is his current stool pale, greasy, or foul-smelling? Also, does he have a visible perineal mass, and are his urine and tears yellow?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cystic Fibrosis. The combination of abdominal distension, feeding difficulties, and abnormal stool passage in an 8-month-old is highly suggestive of meconium ileus or distal intestinal obstruction caused by pancreatic insufficiency and thick secretions.
